newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Active Australian stocks slide to lower close.
newsitem.headline: Active Australian stocks slide to lower close.

text.p: An active Australian sharemarket slid to a lower close on Wednesday, the market following the Dow down early and quickly settling in about 10 points lower.
By the close, the All Ordinaries index lost 9.4 points to stand at 2,370.7.
While the day's end result showed a loss, brokers were heartened by the local bourse's relatively muted response to Wall Street's 1.2 percent loss.
Turnover topped A$1.2 billion, reflecting what brokers said was a surprisingly active day with solid investor interest.
"It was a very good performance. Everyone was expecting a much duller day than it has turned out to be," said Kevin Lourey of Melbourne-based brokerage, Peake Lands Kirwan.
Topping turnover was ANZ Bank with its attractive dividend yield seen as the lure for buyers despite previous takeover speculation. Over 43 million ANZ Bank shares were traded.
"I believe it is the yield. There is perennial talk of ANZ being in line for takeover, but that won't happen until Wallis has reported."
The Federal government-appointed Wallis inquiry into the financial system is due to conclude in March 1997.

Other stocks under the spotlight included oil and gas explorer, Bligh Oil and Minerals, whose scrip soared 48 percent to A$0.51 (US$0.41), their highest level in nearly seven years, as traders digested Tuesday's report of the discovery of a major gas zone in its exploration areas in Texas.

On the downside, shares in Perth-based computer group Formulab Neuronetics slumped 20 percent to A$0.94 as profit takers, tempted by the strong gains of the last month, cashed in after the U.S. launch of the Richter Paradigm Computer.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about seven to five, while about 27 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
